background: Retry failed payment captures automatically, or leave them for support?
intuitive: When a card is charged but our confirmation never arrives, someone has to decide whether the machine or a human retries it.
why: Auto-retry can double-charge if the first capture actually succeeded; leaving them costs about 40 support tickets a week.
rec: Auto-retry, but only where the gateway returned a network timeout - that is the one case we can prove was never captured.
diagram:
capture sent
       |
       v
  no reply ---> timeout?
       |            |
     other        yes -> retry
       |
       v
   support queue

what: Backfill 90 days of capture logs into the new ledger table
intuitive: Copying old payment records into the new format so the reports cover history, not just today.
progress: 38 of 90 days copied, 2.1M rows, no mismatches so far

intuitive: Actually taking the money that was set aside when the card was authorised.
technical: The second leg of a two-phase card payment: authorisation reserves funds, capture settles them. A capture can time out after the funds have already moved.

background: Ship the ledger migration behind a flag, or all at once?
why: A bad migration is hard to reverse once reports read from it.
